svg.title: State count, not bandwidth, is the hard limit: three constrained resources and the arithmetic of a 2.5x oversubscription
svg.desc: Three constrained resources at the top: mroute entries limited by TCAM or a hash table, where exceeding it means new groups cannot be created while old ones keep working; outgoing interface list length limited by the replication engine, where exceeding it silently drops one branch; and replication bandwidth limited by the fabric, where exceeding it degrades packets. Middle: the estimation formulas - PIM-SM with switchover is (*,G) plus (S,G) and grows with receiver subtrees, SSM is (S,G) with no (*,G), bidirectional is (*,G) only and constant regardless of sources. Bottom: a worked capacity judgement - a platform supporting 32K mroutes with 32 interfaces per entry, against a service of 2,000 groups times 40 branches, equals 80K entries, 2.5 times over. The answer is architectural: MVR aggregation, per-region channel partitioning, SSM to remove (*,G), and bidirectional where necessary.
svg.text: Three resources are limited at the same time
Bandwidth is the number people plan. State is the number that decides whether the design can exist at all.
Limit: hardware TCAM, or a software
New groups cannot be created. Old ones
keep working: "new channels will not open".
Excess interfaces are dropped. One branch
is silently missing, and only that branch.
are lost - the classic "it works off-peak".
HOW TO ESTIMATE IT BEFORE YOU BUY ANYTHING
grows with receiver subtrees, not receivers: 100 viewers on one LAN = 1 (S,G)
no (*,G) and no register state, so the RP cannot affect it
constant regardless of how many sources publish
The unit you must write into the design is entries per node, per PIM mode, at peak, plus the OIL width per entry.
A design that only lists Mbps has not been sized. A design that lists entries has.
Tuning does not close a 2.5x gap.
The OIL fits (40 > 32 is already close), the
entries do not. Both must be checked.
1. MVR aggregation: carry one copy per
VLAN instead of one per channel.
Each one changes the tree shape, not a knob.
